etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English momelen, a frequentative of mum (sense 3) (“silent”). Compare German mümmeln, Middle Dutch mommelen and Dutch mompelen.

definitions.definition: (transitive, intransitive) To speak unintelligibly or inaudibly; to fail to articulate.

quote.citation: c. 1591–1595 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Tragedie of Romeo and Ivliet”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene v]:

quote.text: A wrinkled hag, with age grown double, / Picking dry sticks, and mumbling to herself.

definitions.definition: To chew something gently with closed lips.
A quiet or unintelligible vocalization; a low tone of voice.
